steps.instructions: Verify the physical network connection at the approved analyzer or system-control connection point. Inspect accessible Ethernet cabling for damage or loose connectors. Check available port-link indicators. Coordinate with IT to confirm the assigned switch port and network service are operational. Do not change IP addresses, VLAN assignments, or interface settings without authorization. Expected outcome: The external network path is physically connected and its operational status is verified.

steps.title: 6. Coordinate an End-to-End Interface Check
steps.instructions: Have IT or the LIS interface team review the relevant host connection and message queues. Determine whether results are leaving the Alinity c interface. Check whether the interface engine receives and accepts the messages. Confirm that specimen identifiers, test mappings, and receiving-system rules are valid. Review available rejection or acknowledgment information. Avoid repeated retransmission until duplicate-result handling is established. Expected outcome: The failure is localized to analyzer release, transmission, interface processing, or LIS acceptance.

steps.title: 7. Verify Result Delivery After Correction
steps.instructions: Use an approved test transaction or laboratory-authorized specimen workflow. Confirm that the result leaves the analyzer. Verify receipt and correct association with the intended specimen in the LIS. Confirm test identity, units, status, and relevant flags remain intact. Have laboratory personnel reconcile any outstanding results. Expected outcome: Results transmit accurately and appear in the correct LIS records. Troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 8. Escalate Persistent Interface Problems
steps.instructions: If physical communication is verified but messages still fail, coordinate further investigation with Abbott, IT, and the LIS vendor. Preserve event logs and interface timestamps. Keep the affected interface out of clinical use until controlled reporting is restored. Expected outcome: The unresolved communication fault is assigned to the appropriate support team.

CCR.Complaint: Laboratory staff reported that completed Alinity c chemistry results were not appearing in the LIS despite acceptable calibration and QC.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found that the external Ethernet connection at the system-control workstation was disconnected.
CCR.Resolution: The network cable was securely reconnected, communication status recovered, and laboratory personnel verified successful delivery of an authorized test result to the correct LIS record.

title: Abbott Alinity c Clinical Chemistry Analyzer - Cuvette Supply, Loader, or Reaction-Vessel Sensor Reports Empty
description: Investigate reported reaction-vessel or cuvette availability faults involving consumable status, carousel positioning, accessible sensors, or loading-system configuration.

steps.title: 1. Protect Testing and Stop Unsafe Movement
steps.instructions: Notify laboratory personnel that reaction-vessel availability cannot be confirmed. Suspend affected sample processing and arrange alternate validated testing when necessary. Do not manually move reaction mechanisms while the analyzer is active. Do not place hands or tools into guarded carousel mechanisms. Do not bypass consumable or sensor alarms. Expected outcome: Testing is safely interrupted while the reported vessel-availability problem is investigated.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Exact Reported Condition
steps.instructions: Record the full Alinity c alarm message and event timestamp. Determine whether the message identifies cuvette availability, a cuvette segment, reaction-carousel positioning, or another supply or sensor function. Confirm which module and physical subsystem are affected. Verify the actual consumable and vessel-handling configuration before assuming a separate cuvette supply loader is installed. Review whether the fault appeared during startup, washing, or routine processing. Expected outcome: The reported condition is associated with the correct Alinity c subsystem rather than an assumed loader mechanism.

steps.title: 3. Verify Cuvette and Reaction-Carousel Status
steps.instructions: Review normal system displays for cuvette, segment, or reaction-carousel status. Determine whether the instrument reports an unavailable, missing, or improperly positioned reaction-vessel component. Check whether the fault followed approved maintenance or consumable handling. Do not manually install or remove internal cuvette segments unless the specific task is authorized by Abbott documentation and the laboratory's procedures. Expected outcome: The reported vessel condition is confirmed through the instrument's approved status information.

steps.title: 4. Inspect Accessible Areas for Obstructions
steps.instructions: Place the analyzer in the manufacturer-approved safe state. Visually inspect accessible areas associated with the reported fault. Look for foreign objects, spills, misplaced material, or visible damage. Do not reach beneath protective covers or move the carousel manually. Record any signs of physical interference. Expected outcome: No accessible foreign material or obstruction is present, or a condition requiring service is identified.

steps.title: 5. Review Recent Maintenance or Handling
steps.instructions: Ask laboratory personnel whether cuvette-related maintenance, cleaning, or inspection occurred before the problem. Check whether an approved procedure was interrupted or left incomplete. Confirm that accessible covers and service access points are properly secured. Do not attempt to reset sensor positions or alter mechanical alignment. Expected outcome: Any incomplete approved maintenance process is identified without disturbing internal mechanisms.

steps.title: 6. Check Associated Operating Alarms
steps.instructions: Review the event log for reaction-carousel, cuvette-wash, positioning, or initialization errors. Determine whether a related alarm occurred before the empty indication. Check for any accompanying abnormal mechanical noise. Avoid treating a secondary empty indication as proof of depleted consumables. Expected outcome: The relationship between the reported empty condition and other instrument faults is understood.

steps.title: 7. Perform Approved Recovery and Verification
steps.instructions: If an external issue has been corrected and no damage is suspected, perform the manufacturer-approved recovery process. Observe whether normal cuvette or reaction-carousel status is restored. Allow the instrument to complete its required checks. Have laboratory personnel run the appropriate functional checks and QC. Confirm that the fault does not recur. Expected outcome: The vessel-handling status is normal, required checks are successful, and QC is acceptable. Troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 8. Escalate Unresolved Sensor or Carousel Problems
steps.instructions: If the empty indication persists or mechanical motion is abnormal, stop further recovery attempts. Preserve alarm history and observations. Request Abbott service evaluation. Expected outcome: The unresolved issue is transferred for qualified diagnosis without additional mechanical risk.

CCR.Complaint: Laboratory staff reported a reaction-vessel availability message following routine cleaning of the Alinity c.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found that an accessible cover associated with the approved maintenance area had not been fully closed after cleaning.
CCR.Resolution: The cover was properly secured, the approved initialization completed without the availability alarm, and laboratory personnel verified acceptable operational checks and QC.

title: Abbott Alinity c Clinical Chemistry Analyzer - ISE Module Calibration, Reference Solution, or Electrolyte Result Is Unstable
description: Troubleshoot unstable electrolyte measurements or calibration failures involving ISE-related solutions, consumables, sample quality, and operating conditions.

steps.title: 1. Protect Electrolyte Result Accuracy
steps.instructions: Notify laboratory personnel that affected electrolyte results may be unreliable. Suspend impacted assays until required calibration and QC are acceptable. Redirect urgent testing to another validated analyzer. Ask the laboratory to assess previously reported results if the failure may have affected patient testing. Do not release results using failed or unstable ISE calibration. Expected outcome: Affected electrolyte testing is isolated and clinical testing continuity is maintained.

steps.title: 2. Identify the Affected Electrolyte Measurement
steps.instructions: Review the Alinity c calibration and QC history. Determine whether sodium, potassium, chloride, or multiple ISE measurements are affected. Record the exact error or instability pattern. Compare current results with recent calibration and QC trends. Determine whether instability began after maintenance, reagent replacement, or a prolonged analyzer interruption. Expected outcome: The scope and timing of the electrolyte measurement problem are established.

steps.title: 3. Verify ISE-Related Consumables
steps.instructions: Have laboratory personnel inspect the applicable ISE reference and other required solutions. Verify correct product identification, installation, expiration, and remaining availability. Check for leaks, loose accessible connections, or improperly installed consumables. Confirm storage and handling requirements were met. Do not substitute nonapproved solutions. Expected outcome: Required ISE consumables are correct, available, and properly installed.

steps.title: 4. Review Recent Consumable Changes
steps.instructions: Determine whether the problem began after an ISE-related solution or consumable was replaced. Confirm that the appropriate approved replacement procedure was completed. Review any system messages indicating that an associated initialization, preparation, or calibration step remains incomplete. Do not manually manipulate internal electrodes or fluid paths. Expected outcome: The consumable replacement history is verified and no required approved preparation step remains outstanding.

steps.title: 5. Evaluate Sample and QC Material Conditions
steps.instructions: Have laboratory personnel verify the identity and suitability of calibrators and QC material. Check lot information, expiration, handling, and preparation requirements. Review sample conditions for hemolysis, contamination, inappropriate containers, or other known preanalytical problems. Compare the affected channel's QC trend with other electrolyte channels. Do not change clinical acceptance criteria to force a passing result. Expected outcome: Sample-related and control-material causes are ruled out or identified.

steps.title: 6. Check External Operating Conditions
steps.instructions: Review any water, waste, temperature, or related fluid-system alarms. Confirm environmental conditions do not suggest overheating, freezing, leakage, or an interrupted supply. Verify that the analyzer has completed its normal operating initialization. Document any abnormal conditions rather than adjusting internal temperature or sensing components. Expected outcome: No unresolved external or environmental condition is interfering with ISE operation.

steps.title: 7. Perform Laboratory-Approved Calibration and QC
steps.instructions: After any authorized external correction, have laboratory personnel complete the applicable Abbott calibration process. Review calibration acceptance status. Run the required QC materials. Evaluate whether results are stable and meet the laboratory's established criteria. Do not repeatedly recalibrate to conceal a persistent underlying problem. Expected outcome: Calibration is accepted and electrolyte QC is stable. Troubleshooting can stop when the laboratory approves the affected assays for patient use.

steps.title: 8. Escalate Unstable Measurements
steps.instructions: If instability persists despite verified consumables and QC materials, remove affected testing from service. Preserve calibration curves or available reports, QC trends, and event history. Contact Abbott technical support for further evaluation. Expected outcome: The unresolved electrolyte measurement issue is documented and escalated appropriately.

CCR.Complaint: Laboratory staff reported unstable sodium QC results and repeated ISE calibration difficulties.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering and laboratory personnel found that the installed ISE reference solution was expired.
CCR.Resolution: Laboratory personnel replaced the expired solution with an approved in-date product, completed the required preparation and calibration, and verified acceptable sodium QC.

helpfulDetails: Calibration results before and after correction

title: Abbott Alinity c Clinical Chemistry Analyzer - Reaction Carousel or Incubation Temperature Is Out of Range
description: Investigate reaction carousel and incubation temperature faults associated with ventilation, environmental conditions, startup stabilization, or temperature-control abnormalities.

steps.title: 1. Protect Patient Testing
steps.instructions: Notify laboratory personnel of the temperature-related fault. Suspend affected testing when reaction temperature cannot be maintained within manufacturer requirements. Arrange alternate validated testing for time-sensitive specimens. Do not override temperature alarms or accept potentially unreliable assay results. Coordinate review of results produced during the affected period. Expected outcome: Testing is contained until the required reaction temperature can be verified.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Temperature Fault
steps.instructions: Record the exact Alinity c error message. Identify whether the alarm involves the reaction carousel, incubation system, or another temperature-controlled area. Record the displayed temperature and status information available through normal system functions. Determine whether the fault occurs during startup, after extended operation, or intermittently. Review the event history for related operating alarms. Expected outcome: The affected temperature-control function and failure pattern are identified.

steps.title: 3. Check Room Environmental Conditions
steps.instructions: Verify the laboratory temperature is within the manufacturer's approved operating range. Look for recent HVAC interruptions, abnormal room heating, or direct exposure to conditioned-air discharge. Identify nearby equipment that may be adding excessive heat. Coordinate environmental corrections with facilities personnel. Avoid inventing or substituting temperature limits for Abbott specifications. Expected outcome: The analyzer is operating in an appropriate laboratory environment.

steps.title: 4. Inspect External Ventilation and Clearance
steps.instructions: Inspect accessible ventilation openings for dust accumulation or obstruction. Verify that carts, boxes, supplies, or adjacent equipment are not restricting airflow. Listen for unusual fan noise without opening protected covers. Check for visible accumulation around accessible cooling areas. Clean only approved external surfaces using permitted methods. Expected outcome: External airflow is unobstructed and no obvious ventilation problem is present. If an external obstruction is corrected and temperature stabilizes with accepted QC, troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 5. Review Startup and Stabilization Conditions
steps.instructions: Determine whether the analyzer was recently powered down or restarted. Review whether sufficient manufacturer-defined stabilization time has elapsed. Check whether the analyzer reports an ongoing readiness or temperature-stabilization condition. Do not repeatedly cycle power to force readiness. Do not adjust internal heaters, sensors, or temperature setpoints. Expected outcome: The temperature status is evaluated under the correct operating and stabilization conditions.

steps.title: 6. Check for Related System Faults
steps.instructions: Review active instrument messages for power, cooling, fan, or initialization-related problems. Verify that external power remains stable. Check whether the problem appeared after service, relocation, or environmental changes. Document any correlation with abnormal operation. Expected outcome: External power and operating conditions are verified, and associated alarms are identified.

steps.title: 7. Verify Temperature Recovery
steps.instructions: After an approved external correction, monitor the normal instrument temperature-status display. Confirm the instrument reaches and maintains its required operating condition. Have laboratory personnel complete applicable functional checks, calibration, and QC. Verify that the temperature alarm does not return during the approved observation period. Expected outcome: Reaction temperature remains acceptable and required laboratory checks pass. Troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 8. Escalate Persistent Temperature Faults
steps.instructions: If the instrument cannot reach or maintain its required temperature under appropriate environmental conditions, stop affected testing. Preserve temperature trends and event messages. Request Abbott service evaluation. Expected outcome: The unresolved thermal-control problem is isolated for qualified service.

CCR.Complaint: Laboratory staff reported repeated reaction temperature alarms during extended Alinity c operation.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found that supply boxes had been placed against the analyzer's external ventilation openings.
CCR.Resolution: The obstructing boxes were removed, normal ventilation clearance was restored, and the analyzer maintained acceptable temperature status and passed laboratory QC.

title: Abbott Alinity c Clinical Chemistry Analyzer - Reaction-Cuvette Wash, Water, or Waste Fault Stops Processing
description: Troubleshoot processing interruptions associated with cuvette washing, inadequate water supply, wash consumables, waste drainage, or external fluid connections.

steps.title: 1. Protect Patient Testing and Contain Fluid Hazards
steps.instructions: Notify laboratory personnel that the analyzer has stopped processing. Redirect urgent specimens to another validated analyzer when necessary. Do not restart processing while water supply or waste management is unreliable. Use appropriate protective equipment when inspecting potentially contaminated waste connections. If liquid is leaking near electrical components, isolate the equipment safely and request authorized service. Expected outcome: Patient testing continuity is maintained and fluid-related hazards are controlled.

steps.title: 2. Identify the Reported Fluid-System Fault
steps.instructions: Review active Alinity c alarms and event history. Determine whether the interruption relates to water supply, cuvette washing, wash solution, waste drainage, or liquid handling. Record when the alarm occurred and which process was active. Determine whether the failure followed maintenance, consumable replacement, plumbing work, or an unexpected facility water interruption. Expected outcome: The affected fluid-system function and timing are identified.

steps.title: 3. Verify External Water Supply
steps.instructions: Confirm that the analyzer's approved water source is available. Check accessible supply-line connections for loose fittings, kinks, compression, or leaks. Verify that the water purification or supply system reports normal status. Coordinate with laboratory or facilities personnel to confirm water quality and availability according to Abbott requirements. Do not bypass water-quality safeguards. Expected outcome: The analyzer receives an appropriate, uninterrupted external water supply.

steps.title: 4. Inspect Wash Solutions and Consumables
steps.instructions: Verify the presence and correct installation of applicable wash and cleaning solutions. Check for empty containers, incorrect products, or visible leakage. Confirm the installed consumables are approved for the system. Check whether a recent consumable replacement introduced the fault. Expected outcome: Required wash consumables are correctly installed and available.

steps.title: 5. Inspect External Waste Connections
steps.instructions: Verify that the waste path is connected to the designated disposal system. Check accessible tubing for kinks, compression, disconnections, or visible leakage. Confirm that applicable waste containers are not full. Check for drainage restrictions that can be identified without disconnecting contaminated internal plumbing. Coordinate facility drain problems with the appropriate support department. Expected outcome: Waste can leave the analyzer through the approved disposal path without visible obstruction or leakage.

steps.title: 6. Inspect the Accessible Cuvette-Wash Area
steps.instructions: Place the system in the approved safe state before inspection. Look for obvious spills, residual liquid, damaged accessible components, or foreign material. Do not reach into a moving reaction carousel or washing mechanism. Do not disassemble internal pumps, valves, wash stations, or manifolds. Record any visible abnormalities for Abbott service personnel. Expected outcome: No accessible obstruction or leak is identified, or a condition requiring service is documented.

steps.title: 7. Verify Recovery After External Correction
steps.instructions: After correcting an approved external issue, perform the manufacturer-authorized recovery procedure. Observe water and waste status during system initialization. Confirm the cuvette-wash-related error clears. Have laboratory personnel perform the required instrument checks and QC. Check for repeated leaks or alarms during the verification process. Expected outcome: Fluid status remains normal, processing resumes, and required QC passes. Troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 8. Escalate Recurring Wash or Fluid Faults
steps.instructions: If water and waste connections are verified but faults continue, stop affected testing. Preserve the event history and observations. Request Abbott service evaluation. Expected outcome: An unresolved fluid-system problem is isolated for qualified service.

CCR.Complaint: Laboratory staff reported that the Alinity c stopped processing and displayed a waste-related fault.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found an externally accessible waste drain hose compressed behind the analyzer.
CCR.Resolution: The hose was repositioned to eliminate the restriction, normal drainage was verified, and the analyzer completed approved functional checks and QC without recurring alarms.

title: Abbott Alinity c Clinical Chemistry Analyzer - Reagent Cartridge Is Loaded but Inventory Is Incorrect
description: Identify reagent inventory discrepancies involving cartridge recognition, incorrect loading, barcode information, reagent status, or inventory synchronization.

steps.title: 1. Protect Testing Accuracy
steps.instructions: Notify laboratory personnel that the affected reagent may not be available for reliable testing. Do not release patient results using a reagent with unresolved identification, expiration, or inventory discrepancies. Arrange alternate validated testing when necessary. Do not manually override reagent identity or expiration controls. Expected outcome: Testing dependent on the questionable reagent is suspended or redirected until inventory accuracy is verified.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Inventory Discrepancy
steps.instructions: Review the reagent inventory display. Identify the affected assay and cartridge. Determine whether the cartridge is missing, assigned to the wrong location, displaying an incorrect quantity, or showing an unexpected lot or expiration. Compare the displayed inventory information with the physical cartridge label and laboratory records. Document any active identification or reagent-management error. Expected outcome: The exact inventory mismatch is identified.

steps.title: 3. Inspect the Physical Reagent Cartridge
steps.instructions: Have authorized laboratory personnel access the cartridge using the approved loading workflow. Verify the cartridge is intended for the Alinity c and the selected assay. Inspect the cartridge for physical damage, leakage, improperly attached labeling, or contamination. Verify lot and expiration information. Confirm appropriate storage and handling requirements were followed. Expected outcome: The cartridge is physically intact, correctly identified, and suitable for use.

steps.title: 4. Verify Cartridge Seating and Loading Position
steps.instructions: Confirm the cartridge occupies the expected reagent location. Check for incomplete seating or interference from surrounding cartridges. Inspect the accessible loading area for foreign material or obstruction. Ensure the access area is properly closed before attempting recognition. Do not manually rotate internal mechanisms or bypass access interlocks. Expected outcome: The reagent cartridge is correctly seated and available for normal identification.

steps.title: 5. Check Reagent Identification and Inventory Updating
steps.instructions: Have laboratory personnel perform the approved reagent loading or inventory update process. Observe whether the system identifies the cartridge correctly. Verify the displayed assay, lot, expiration, and remaining quantity information as applicable. Check for inventory messages involving reagent validity or an unavailable cartridge. Do not edit protected reagent data to force acceptance. Expected outcome: The cartridge is recognized and its displayed inventory agrees with verified cartridge information. If inventory is correct and QC is acceptable, troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 6. Compare With a Known-Good Cartridge
steps.instructions: If permitted by laboratory procedures, use a verified compatible cartridge to determine whether the problem follows the original cartridge. Record whether the replacement is recognized in the applicable loading location. If multiple cartridges fail at the same location, suspect a location-specific identification or loading problem. If only one cartridge fails, isolate that cartridge for laboratory or Abbott evaluation. Expected outcome: The problem is narrowed to a cartridge-specific or instrument-side condition.

steps.title: 7. Verify Reagent Availability and Analytical Readiness
steps.instructions: Confirm that the inventory now reports the correct reagent information. Have laboratory personnel perform applicable calibration and QC requirements. Verify that the affected assay is available without reagent-management alarms. Ensure the laboratory confirms result validity before resuming patient testing. Expected outcome: Inventory is accurate, reagent status is acceptable, and required QC passes. Troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 8. Escalate Persistent Recognition Problems
steps.instructions: If inventory remains incorrect after proper cartridge loading and approved updating, stop using the affected assay or module. Preserve cartridge identification information and error history. Contact Abbott technical support. Expected outcome: The unresolved issue is documented for investigation without introducing incorrect reagent information.

CCR.Complaint: Laboratory staff reported that a newly loaded reagent cartridge was not appearing in the Alinity c inventory.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found that the cartridge was not fully seated in its designated loading position.
CCR.Resolution: Laboratory personnel correctly reseated the cartridge, the instrument recognized its identification and inventory information, and the required QC passed.

title: Abbott Alinity c Clinical Chemistry Analyzer - Reagent Refrigeration Will Not Hold Temperature
description: Identify reagent refrigeration problems involving environmental heat, obstructed ventilation, access conditions, unstable power, or internal cooling faults.

steps.title: 1. Protect Reagent Integrity
steps.instructions: Notify laboratory personnel of the refrigeration problem. Prevent use of reagents whose storage conditions cannot be verified. Have laboratory personnel assess reagent exposure and determine disposition using approved stability requirements. Arrange alternate validated testing when affected reagents cannot be used. Do not assume an expired or temperature-exposed reagent becomes acceptable after refrigeration recovers. Expected outcome: Potentially compromised reagents are isolated from patient testing.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Refrigeration Problem
steps.instructions: Review the Alinity c reagent-temperature status and active alarms. Record available current temperature and event information. Determine whether the temperature is elevated, unstable, or failing to reach the required condition. Identify when the problem began. Check whether it followed power interruption, instrument relocation, service, or prolonged access to the reagent area. Expected outcome: The temperature problem and possible reagent exposure period are established.

steps.title: 3. Verify Laboratory Environmental Conditions
steps.instructions: Confirm the room environment meets manufacturer requirements. Check for excessive ambient heat, direct sunlight, or nearby heat-producing equipment. Review recent HVAC problems with facilities personnel. Determine whether the instrument has adequate surrounding clearance. Expected outcome: External environmental conditions are appropriate for refrigeration operation.

steps.title: 4. Inspect External Cooling and Ventilation
steps.instructions: Check accessible ventilation openings for dust, packaging, or other obstructions. Confirm surrounding equipment is not restricting airflow. Listen for abnormal cooling-system noise without opening protected housings. Do not remove cooling-system guards or disassemble refrigeration components. Document unusual vibration, heat, or sound. Expected outcome: External cooling airflow is unobstructed, and visible abnormalities are documented.

steps.title: 5. Verify Reagent Area Access and Closure
steps.instructions: Have laboratory personnel confirm that the reagent loading area is correctly closed. Inspect accessible covers or closure surfaces for obvious obstruction or damage. Check whether frequent or prolonged loading activity coincides with the temperature problem. Do not bypass access switches, force covers, or defeat safety interlocks. Expected outcome: The reagent area is correctly closed and no accessible condition prevents normal operation.

steps.title: 6. Verify Electrical and Operating Status
steps.instructions: Confirm that the instrument has stable electrical power. Check whether an approved power source or external UPS reports an abnormal condition. Review system messages for cooling, power, or controller-related faults. Avoid repeated shutdowns or power cycling that could worsen temperature instability. Expected outcome: The refrigeration system has stable external power and no unresolved external operating condition is identified.

steps.title: 7. Observe Temperature Recovery
steps.instructions: After correcting an external issue, monitor refrigeration status through normal system displays. Confirm the temperature returns to and remains within Abbott requirements. Have laboratory personnel determine which reagents remain acceptable. Complete applicable calibration and QC before resuming affected testing. Do not return questionable reagents to service solely because the temperature alarm clears. Expected outcome: Refrigeration is stable, reagents are accepted by the laboratory, and required QC passes. Troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 8. Escalate Continued Refrigeration Failure
steps.instructions: If the system cannot maintain the required temperature, stop affected testing. Preserve temperature records and alarm history. Contact Abbott service personnel. Expected outcome: The refrigeration problem is documented and escalated without risking additional reagent use.

CCR.Complaint: Laboratory staff reported that the Alinity c reagent refrigeration temperature remained elevated during normal operation.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found that stored supplies were obstructing the analyzer's external cooling ventilation.
CCR.Resolution: The supplies were relocated, ventilation clearance was restored, refrigeration temperature returned to the approved operating range, and laboratory personnel verified reagent acceptability and QC.

title: Abbott Alinity c Clinical Chemistry Analyzer - Sample Barcode, Carrier Position, or Tube Type Is Misidentified
description: Troubleshoot sample identification problems involving unreadable barcodes, incorrectly positioned carriers, incompatible tubes, or specimen-routing discrepancies.

steps.title: 1. Protect Patient and Specimen Identification
steps.instructions: Notify laboratory personnel that sample identification may be unreliable. Suspend processing of affected specimens until identity and position are confirmed. Do not manually assign specimen identities without the laboratory's approved verification process. Quarantine any potentially misidentified results for laboratory review. Redirect urgent testing when necessary. Expected outcome: No specimen is processed or reported under an unverified patient identity.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Exact Identification Failure
steps.instructions: Review active analyzer messages and sample-processing history. Determine whether the problem involves barcode reading, carrier position, tube recognition, or sample-to-order matching. Record the affected carrier and position. Determine whether the problem affects one specimen, one carrier, or multiple samples. Confirm whether the discrepancy occurs before processing or during result association. Expected outcome: The identification failure and its scope are established.

steps.title: 3. Inspect the Specimen Barcode
steps.instructions: Have laboratory personnel verify the physical specimen label against the laboratory record. Check for wrinkled, damaged, smudged, poorly printed, or incorrectly positioned labels. Look for overlapping labels or labels wrapped around the tube in a way that interferes with scanning. Verify that the barcode format is supported by the configured system. Do not substitute a manually entered identifier without approved verification. Expected outcome: The barcode is readable, correctly positioned, and corresponds to the intended specimen.

steps.title: 4. Verify Tube Type and Carrier Compatibility
steps.instructions: Confirm that the specimen tube is approved for the relevant analyzer configuration. Check tube dimensions, caps, and seating against the laboratory's approved setup. Inspect the carrier for damage, debris, or incorrect positioning. Ensure the tube is securely seated and not tilted. Do not modify carrier components to accommodate unsupported tubes. Expected outcome: The specimen and carrier meet the approved physical configuration.

steps.title: 5. Inspect Accessible Barcode-Reading Areas
steps.instructions: Check for visible dirt, residue, or obstruction at accessible scanning surfaces. Clean only approved external surfaces using the manufacturer's permitted procedure. Do not dismantle scanner hardware or alter optical alignment. Inspect accessible cables and connections when the scanner is an external component. Record any visibly damaged scanner surface or connector. Expected outcome: No external obstruction or connection problem interferes with barcode recognition.

steps.title: 6. Compare With a Verified Specimen and Carrier
steps.instructions: Have laboratory personnel use an authorized test specimen or verified barcode. Determine whether identification succeeds in the affected carrier or position. If appropriate, compare results using another verified carrier. Note whether the failure follows the barcode, tube, carrier, or physical loading position. Do not exchange clinical specimen identities during comparison. Expected outcome: The failure is isolated to specimen labeling, carrier condition, loading position, or scanner function.

steps.title: 7. Verify Sample Identity Through Processing
steps.instructions: After correcting the identified external issue, perform an approved identification check. Confirm that the analyzer displays the correct specimen identifier and position. Have laboratory personnel verify correct order association and downstream result identification. Ensure no unresolved specimen mismatch remains. Expected outcome: Sample identity remains correct from scanning through result association. Troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 8. Escalate Repeated Misidentification
steps.instructions: If validated specimens and carriers continue to produce incorrect identification, stop affected processing. Preserve scanner error history and position information. Contact Abbott technical support and the laboratory informatics team as appropriate. Expected outcome: The unresolved identification issue is isolated without compromising additional specimens.

CCR.Complaint: Laboratory staff reported repeated barcode identification failures for specimens loaded in one Alinity c carrier.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found that the carrier was damaged and allowed specimen tubes to tilt away from the expected scanning position.
CCR.Resolution: The damaged carrier was replaced with an approved compatible carrier, and laboratory personnel verified correct barcode recognition and sample identification through the normal workflow.

helpfulDetails: Identification results before and after correction

title: Abbott Alinity c Clinical Chemistry Analyzer - Sample/Reagent Pipettor Collision, Clot, or Aspiration Error
description: Troubleshoot pipettor collisions, clot detection, and aspiration failures caused by sample tubes, reagent cartridges, obstructions, or external handling conditions.

steps.title: 1. Protect Patient Testing and Stop Unsafe Operation
steps.instructions: Notify laboratory personnel that the affected analyzer may not reliably process specimens. Stop affected testing using the approved laboratory workflow. Arrange testing on another validated analyzer when necessary. Do not attempt to reposition a pipettor while the instrument is operating. Treat all specimens and exposed fluid-path components as potentially biohazardous. If a collision has occurred, do not repeatedly restart movement without identifying the obstruction. Expected outcome: Specimen processing is safely stopped or redirected, and the pipettor is not exposed to additional damage.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Exact Pipettor Error
steps.instructions: Review the Alinity c event history and active error messages. Identify whether the failure involves the sample pipettor, reagent pipettor, or another liquid-handling operation. Determine whether the reported condition is a mechanical collision, clot detection, insufficient aspiration, or liquid-level detection problem. Record the affected specimen, reagent, rack position, and time when available. Determine whether the failure occurs consistently at the same position or intermittently across multiple tests. Expected outcome: The affected pipetting operation and failure pattern are identified.

steps.title: 3. Inspect Sample Tubes and Carrier Positioning
steps.instructions: Verify that the tube or sample container is approved for the configured assay and sampling arrangement. Check for tilted tubes, improperly seated containers, incorrect caps, damaged carriers, or physical obstructions. Confirm the sample is positioned correctly in its assigned carrier. Have laboratory personnel assess specimen volume, clots, fibrin, bubbles, and other sample-quality concerns. Do not manually disturb the specimen or override sample acceptance requirements. Expected outcome: The specimen is correctly positioned and suitable for the intended aspiration operation. If correcting a positioning problem restores verified operation, troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 4. Inspect Reagent Cartridges and Accessible Loading Areas
steps.instructions: Confirm that reagent cartridges are fully seated and correctly positioned. Look for protruding packaging, damaged cartridge housings, displaced containers, or visible spills. Verify that the expected reagent is available in the instrument inventory. Check for any obstruction in the accessible pipettor travel area without entering guarded moving mechanisms. If a cartridge has tipped or leaked inside the reagent area, stop and follow the manufacturer-approved spill and service process. Expected outcome: No cartridge or accessible obstruction interferes with the pipettor path.

steps.title: 5. Check Pipettor Condition Without Manual Adjustment
steps.instructions: With the instrument in the manufacturer-approved safe state, visually inspect accessible probe surfaces. Look for visible bending, residue, dried material, or signs of physical contact. Do not bend, straighten, manually align, or force the pipettor. Do not attempt internal tubing, motor, or alignment repairs. If probe damage is visible, remove the affected module from service. Expected outcome: No visible pipettor damage is present, or suspected damage is identified for qualified service evaluation.

steps.title: 6. Verify Consumables and Operating Conditions
steps.instructions: Check applicable wash solution, cleaning solution, water supply, and waste status. Review whether the analyzer reports liquid-handling pressure, aspiration, or wash-related faults. Confirm appropriate reagent availability and that no required consumable is depleted. Review whether a recent reagent or consumable change immediately preceded the error. Expected outcome: External liquid-handling supplies and consumables are available, correctly installed, and free of reported faults.

steps.title: 7. Perform an Approved Functional Check
steps.instructions: Once external problems are corrected, allow the analyzer to complete the applicable manufacturer-approved recovery or initialization process. Observe the affected pipetting operation through normal guarded operation. Have laboratory personnel perform the appropriate system checks, calibration, and QC as required. Verify that no collision, clot, or aspiration errors recur. Expected outcome: The pipettor completes its operating sequence without errors and the laboratory accepts the verification results. Troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 8. Escalate Repeated Failures
steps.instructions: If errors recur with correctly positioned specimens and verified consumables, stop testing on the affected module. Preserve the event history and affected-position information. Contact Abbott technical support or authorized service personnel. Expected outcome: The unresolved fault is documented and transferred for manufacturer-level evaluation without additional mechanical damage.

CCR.Complaint: Laboratory staff reported repeated sample pipettor collision errors when processing a specific specimen rack.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found a sample tube improperly seated in its carrier, allowing it to protrude into the pipettor travel path.
CCR.Resolution: The tube was correctly seated by laboratory personnel, the approved recovery sequence completed successfully, and subsequent functional checks and QC passed without additional errors.
